name: duna: transcripción en directo
oneLine: A free Spanish app for iPhone and Mac that writes speech down on the device, with no internet after a one-time download, in Spanish, Catalan, English, Galician and Basque, made so the text holds still while you read.

platforms.detail: One free download gives you the iPhone app and the Mac app. Each device transcribes on its own and nothing travels between them. A Google Play search finds no duna app.

deviceRequirements.text: iOS 26 or later; Mac: M1 or later, macOS 26
deviceRequirements.detail: An iPhone on iOS 26 or later, or a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) on macOS 26 or later. Each language takes 120 to 195 MB of space.

roomCaptions.detail: Put the iPhone on the table between you and the speaker, tap anywhere on the screen and read. It works with the iPhone's own microphone, a wired one or Bluetooth headphones.

groupConversations.text: New paragraph when the voice changes
groupConversations.detail: When a different person starts speaking, duna usually begins a new paragraph. It does not say who is speaking, and it warns that several people talking at once causes more mistakes.

languages.detail: You choose one language per session and download it once. Galician and Basque are marked New: they are the most recent and make more mistakes. The Catalan voice model comes from the Barcelona Supercomputing Center (Projecte Aina) and the Basque one from HiTZ (UPV/EHU).

offline.text: Yes, after a one-time language download
offline.detail: Internet is only needed to download a language. After that, listening, transcribing and making subtitles all work offline, also in airplane mode.

speakerLabels.text: No names or labels; new paragraph per voice
speakerLabels.detail: duna detects that the voice has changed only to start a new paragraph. Its privacy policy says it does not identify who is speaking.

voiceNames.detail: The privacy policy says duna does not identify who speaks, creates no voiceprint and keeps nothing from the analysis of voice changes.

speakerDirection.detail: The iPhone guide says an orb at the top moves with the voices it hears; a direction for each voice is not described.

translation.detail: Its pages describe transcription in the one language you choose per session, with no translation.

saveTranscripts.text: Yes, text on the device; no sync
saveTranscripts.detail: Every session you stop is kept in duna's folder, listed by day with a search, where you can give it a title, correct the text and export it. No audio is recorded to a file, and transcripts don't sync between the iPhone and the Mac.

export.detail: Exports a transcript as plain text, Markdown or .srt subtitles timed word by word, to Notes, Files, AirDrop or any app. Video subtitles can be exported burnt into a copy of the video, which goes straight to Photos on the iPhone.

fileUpload.text: Video and audio files, on the device
fileUpload.detail: Choose a video or audio file, say which language is spoken, and duna writes .srt subtitles on the device, then opens a line-by-line editor. A 15-minute episode takes under a minute on a recent Mac, a little longer on an iPhone.

customWords.detail: Add the day's names, places, brands and acronyms. duna favours them while it listens, and a change applies at once, even mid-session.

display.text: Text holds still; large type, 4 fonts, light or dark
display.detail: Lines you have read never move: the newest line stays at the same height and older lines roll up. Type goes from comfortable to huge, in four typefaces, two of them (Atkinson Hyperlegible) designed for low vision, in light or dark mode. Three profiles trade steadiness for speed.

soundAlerts.detail: Its pages don't describe alerts for sounds like a doorbell or an alarm.

phoneCalls.detail: Its pages describe speech in the room and saved files, not phone calls.

mediaOnDevice.text: Saved video and audio files only
mediaOnDevice.detail: It makes subtitles for a video or audio file you already have, including one shared to it from Photos, Files or another app. Captioning sound as it plays on the device is not described.

humanCaptioners.detail: duna says it is an automatic transcription that makes mistakes and does not replace professional captioning or interpreting.

privacy.text: On the device; nothing is sent
privacy.detail: Voice, text and videos are processed on the iPhone or Mac and never sent anywhere. No audio is saved to a file. Its only internet use is downloading languages, from Apple or, as a fallback, from a copy on GitHub. The App Store privacy label says no data is collected.

account.detail: No accounts, no ads and no tracking.

availability.text: App Store: Spain, Mexico and more
availability.detail: Listed on the Spanish and Mexican App Stores (November 2026). The app and the website are in Catalan, Spanish and English, and the app's menus also in Galician and Basque. Not on Google Play.

freePlan.detail: Every feature is free on the iPhone and the Mac, with no limit described.

price.detail: No subscription, no in-app purchases and no ads (Spanish App Store and duna's terms, November 2026).

strengths.text: Free with every feature, on both the iPhone and the Mac, with no subscription, in-app purchases, ads or account.
Speech is turned into text on the device and nothing is sent anywhere; after a one-time language download it works in airplane mode.
Captions Catalan, Galician and Basque as well as Spanish and English.
Makes .srt subtitles for videos on the device, with a line-by-line editor and an export of the video with the subtitles burnt in.

limits.text: Needs iOS 26 on iPhone or an Apple silicon Mac on macOS 26; there is no Android app.
One language per session, five in all; Galician and Basque make more mistakes.
It starts a new paragraph when the voice changes but does not say who is speaking.
Transcripts stay on the device where they were made and don't sync between the iPhone and the Mac.

notes: Developer: Oriol O'Callaghan (signs as Uri O'Callaghan on the support page), an individual, not a company, in Sant Cugat del Vallès (Barcelona, Catalonia), per the legal notice and the App Store trader details. Released 12 Oct 2026 (App Store version history shows 1.0 on 16 Oct and 1.1 on 21 Oct 2026). Platforms: the Spanish App Store page shows 'iPhone, Mac'; the lookup's device list also includes iPads, but the listing is not marked universal and duna's own pages only name iPhone and Mac, so iPad is left out. Languages: the App Store 'languages' field (EU, CA, EN, GL, ES) is the app's own menus; the caption languages are the same five (one per session). Speech models named in the terms: Catalan from the Barcelona Supercomputing Center (Projecte Aina), Spanish and English from NVIDIA, Galician from the BSC, Basque from HiTZ (UPV/EHU); voice-change detection with pyannote. The Spanish and English overview pages say the same things; the root page (duna.uriocallaghan.com) is English, the /es/ page Spanish. The site also has Catalan and English versions of the legal pages (not cited). Free: the terms say no in-app purchases or subscriptions; the App Store page data shows hasInAppPurchases false for duna. Availability: the lookup API returned the app in Spain, Mexico, Argentina, the US, the UK, France, Germany and Slovenia, not Andorra (2026-11-02); only ES and MX are cited. Google Play: searches for the exact name, the developer and 'uriocallaghan' return no results; play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.uriocallaghan.duna returns 404. Not stated: translation, summaries, sound alerts, speaker direction, calls, sign language. No press found by web search. Ratings not used. All pages opened 2026-11-02 with curl.
